bounded_statement: Within the supplied files for case:56e4106c5ef7a44d29c8, the selected result (two-sided Fisher exact test on 16 chamber deployments, odds ratio 21.00, p = 0.0406) is produced by entering all 16 deployment rows into a 2x2 Fisher exact test as independent trials, even though the data description designates collar_id as the independent unit and each of the 6 collars contributes 2-3 repeated deployment rows. The Fisher exact test assumes each counted trial is independent, so the repeated entries from the same collar inflate the effective sample size from 6 collars to 16 rows; a collar-level 3-vs-3 comparison cannot reach p < 0.05 under any outcome (minimum two-sided Fisher p = 0.1 for complete separation), so the reported significance depends entirely on the repeated per-collar entries.

counterevidence_considered.description: The report is transparent about the repeated-visit structure: it states that every collar was visited on more than one survey week and provides a per-collar deployment table, so the dependence is disclosed rather than hidden. Disclosure, however, does not make the Fisher exact test's independence assumption hold.

def split_counts(rows, status):
    subset = [row for row in rows if row["drainage_status"] == status]
    hits = sum(1 for row in subset if row["ebullition_detected"] == DETECTED)
    return hits, len(subset) - hits

hit_i, miss_i = split_counts(rows, "intact")
    hit_d, miss_d = split_counts(rows, "drained")
    n_i = hit_i + miss_i
    n_d = hit_d + miss_d
    n_total = n_i + n_d
    _, p_value = fisher_exact([[hit_i, miss_i], [hit_d, miss_d]],
                              alternative="two-sided")

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I tried to defeat the finding two ways. (1) Alternative reading that rows are legitimately independent: the description explicitly designates collar_id as the independent-unit column, states the same collar appears in several rows, and drainage_status is fixed per collar block, so repeated rows from one collar are repeated measurements of one unit within one treatment cell; the row-independence assumption of Fisher's exact test cannot be defended from the supplied files. (2) Robustness check at the declared unit level: with only 3 intact and 3 drained collars, the most extreme possible collar-level 2x2 table ([[3,0],[0,3]]) has a two-sided Fisher exact p of C(3,3)*C(3,0)/C(6,3)*2 = 2/20 = 0.10, so no collar-level dichotomization of these data can reach p < 0.05. The reported p = 0.0406 is therefore attributable to counting 16 dependent rows as trials rather than to information available at the 6 independent units. I also verified the arithmetic pipeline: the CSV yields 7/1 intact and 2/6 drained row-level counts, matching the report's table, odds ratio (7*6)/(1*2) = 21.00, and 16 total rows, confirming the selected result flows from the row-level pooling in split_counts.

root_cause: The workflow's split_counts function pools every CSV row by drainage_status into the 2x2 contingency table without any aggregation to the collar_id level, and compose() feeds those pooled row counts directly into scipy.stats.fisher_exact. Because drainage_status is a fixed property of each collar and each collar appears in 2-3 rows (repeated survey weeks), the same independent unit enters the row-independent Fisher exact procedure multiple times, which the report then explicitly frames as 16 independent trials.
